title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
abstract: arXiv:2611.17015v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how biological research is done. Biological foundation models trained on millions of nucleotides, protein, and single-cell measurements predict protein structures, mutation effects, and cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Agentic systems, AI assistants built on large language models, can run multistep analyses from plain-language requests and increasingly call foundation models as tools. Yet it is often unclear when these models' outputs can be trusted. We frame this as a model's knowledge boundary: the range of inputs, tasks, and conditions over which its outputs are reliable. This review explains how foundation models are built and proposes that five design elements (data, architecture, training scheme, evaluation scheme, and post-analysis) define this boundary. translated_title: 面向生物学家的AI：智能体系统时代的基础模型知识边界
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）正在改变生物学研究的方式。基于数百万核苷酸、蛋白质和单细胞测量数据训练的生物学基础模型，能够预测蛋白质结构、突变效应以及细胞对基因扰动的响应。智能体系统——基于大语言模型构建的AI助手——能够根据自然语言请求执行多步骤分析，并越来越多地将基础模型作为工具加以调用。然而，这些模型的输出何时可以信赖往往并不清楚。我们将这一问题定义为模型的知识边界：即其输出保持可靠的输入、任务和条件范围。本综述阐述了基础模型的构建方式，并提出五个设计要素（数据、架构、训练方案、评估方案和后分析）共同定义了这一边界。我们考察了现有模型在哪些方面成功或失败的证据，并给出了模型局限性的标准化描述，以便研究者……
tldr: 本综述提出“知识边界”这一概念框架，指出数据、架构、训练方案、评估方案和后分析五个设计要素共同决定了生物学基础模型输出可信的范围，为生物学家规范地理解和描述模型及智能体系统的能力局限提供了依据。
en_tdlr: This review introduces the concept of "knowledge boundaries" for biological foundation models, proposing that five design elements—data, architecture, training scheme, evaluation scheme, and post-analysis—define the range over which model outputs are reliable, enabling standardized descriptions of model limits for biologists and agentic systems.
